name: Orange peel teeth whitening

lead: Orange peel whitening is rubbing the inside of an orange or other citrus peel on the teeth to brighten them. Fans like it because it is cheap and natural.
No clinical studies of the practice were found. The peel is rich in limonene oil, but encyclopedic sources do not list tooth whitening among its uses.

paras: Proponents say limonene or fruit acids lift surface stains. No published research tests this.
Dental sources associate acidic fruit and juice exposure with enamel erosion, which is irreversible. Specific data on peel contact are not available.

lead: Orange peel teeth whitening is a home practice of rubbing the inner side of an orange or other citrus peel on the teeth to make them look whiter. It is shared online as a natural, inexpensive alternative to commercial whitening products.

Orange peel contains aromatic oils, of which sweet orange oil is about 90% D-limonene, a compound that is also used as a solvent in household cleaners [1]. The orange itself contains citric acid; dental sources list orange juice among dietary items associated with dental erosion [2]. No published clinical studies of rubbing peel on teeth were found.

paras: Practitioners rub the peel, usually the white pith side, against the teeth. Proponents credit limonene or fruit acids for lifting stains. The encyclopedic description of orange peel covers its use in zest, oils, perfumery and aromatherapy and does not list tooth whitening [1].
No studies found. Whitening research in humans concerns peroxide gels and strips, which can cause tooth sensitivity and gum irritation [3].

Dental erosion is the irreversible loss of tooth structure through acids not of bacterial origin; frequent exposure to fruit juices and sucking citrus fruit are discussed as contributing factors [2]. Dentists generally distinguish this from whitening, and eroded enamel can expose the yellower dentin beneath. Limonene is described as skin-irritating in its concentrated oil form [1]. Whether peel contact carries a similar erosion risk has not been measured in the sources reviewed.
The method appears in roundups of natural whitening tricks. No community-sourced material was available for citation here.
